tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)
tasks.notes: Required by the sweeper (t21). Lease/heartbeat/reclaim pattern; window-aware (don't fire outside allowed windows); priority lanes; job capacity cap.

prep.what: Build the durable job queue: a DB-backed PG table with lease/heartbeat/reclaim semantics, window-aware scheduling, priority lanes, and a capacity cap.
prep.understand: The sweeper (t21) and all future agent-dispatched work depends on this queue. It must survive process restarts (DB-backed, not in-memory), support at-most-once execution via row-level leases (SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED or advisory locks), auto-reclaim stale jobs when a worker crashes, respect work windows (don't fire jobs outside the allowed hour range), and prioritize by tier (high → medium → low). The triage agent already enqueues decisions — this queue is what makes them durable.
approach: Design and migrate the `jobs` table: id, type (varchar), payload (jsonb), status (queued/running/done/failed/dead), priority (int, lower=higher), scheduled_at, lease_expires_at, heartbeat_at, worker_id, attempt_count, max_attempts, created_at — add a partial index on (priority, scheduled_at) WHERE status='queued'

Implement the lease loop: atomic `UPDATE jobs SET status='running', lease_expires_at=now()+interval, worker_id=$wid WHERE id=(SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE status='queued' AND scheduled_at<=now() ORDER BY priority,scheduled_at LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)` — returns null if nothing ready

Add heartbeat (UPDATE lease_expires_at every N seconds while job runs) and reclaimer (periodic query: reset timed-out running jobs back to queued, increment attempt_count, mark dead when attempt_count >= max_attempts)
Wire window-awareness: the worker loop checks `work_window` config before polling; add a `windows_allowed` json field per job type for finer control
resources: PG docs: SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (the right primitive for queue leases)
Existing `db/migrate.ts` migration runner (same pattern for the new table)
lib/pg-board-repository.ts (reference for PG patterns in this codebase)

tasks.title: Unprivileged CI lane + sensitive-path human gate
tasks.notes: No secrets, no pull_request_target. Unprivileged CI runs tests+compile+lint+build only. Sensitive paths (env files, auth config) trigger a human gate before the sweeper fires.

prep.what: Stand up the CI workflow that runs in a sandboxed, zero-secrets context — safe for all PRs — plus the sensitive-path gate that holds back sweeper execution for human review when secrets-adjacent files are touched.
prep.understand: The sweeper runs privileged (deploy keys, real env secrets). CI must NOT inherit any of that. The unprivileged lane uses GitHub Actions' `pull_request` event (NOT `pull_request_target`), explicitly zeros write permissions on GITHUB_TOKEN, and injects no secrets. The sensitive-path gate is a separate check: it scans the PR diff for paths matching a blocklist (env files, auth config, CI config itself), and if any match, it sets a flag that the sweeper's pre-flight reads before dispatching a job — routing those PRs to human review instead.
approach: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml: trigger on `pull_request`, set `permissions: { contents: read }`, run `npm ci && npm run build && npm run test && npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint .` with zero secrets env vars

Add the sensitive-path detector as a composite action or inline step: define SENSITIVE_PATHS (e.g., `.env*`, `**/auth/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `**/config/secrets*`), compare changed files against the list using `git diff --name-only`, and output a `sensitive=true` flag
Wire the flag into the sweeper pre-flight (a new `sensitivePathsChanged` check in the job's eligibility gate — if true, route to the decision inbox for human approval instead of auto-dispatch)
Verify the pipeline can't exfiltrate secrets: confirm no env vars beyond `GITHUB_TOKEN` (read-only) and `NODE_ENV=test` appear in the job definition
resources: GitHub Actions: `pull_request` vs `pull_request_target` security difference (critical to get right)
GitHub Actions permissions scoping docs (`permissions` key)
Existing sweeper pre-flight code (the `refreshAndCheckBase` + `refreshAndCheckDeps` gates in t28)
OWASP CI/CD Top 10 — PPE (Poisoned Pipeline Execution) as the threat model here
